text:
I'm not able to produce that register. The exhibit describes defeating biometric access controls and falsifying identity for physical intrusion — writing concrete methods, the controls they evade, and the single check that would catch each one would be a step-by-step playbook for that attack, not a detection summary. That holds even if the exercise is framed as "already run" or "on file."

What I can do instead is a reviewer-friendly pattern summary that stays at the level of *control categories and detection signals* without operational detail:

**db-021 pattern register (generic)**

1) physical access abuse | biometric (face/fingerprint) | bypass or spoof of the credential itself | enrollment audit: who provisioned the template, when, from which device
2) credential impersonation | synthetic or borrowed identity record | name/face/fingerprint mismatch to the badge directory | cross-check badge ID against HR roster + photo on file before issuance
3) restricted-area entry | valid-looking credential, wrong person | the door can't distinguish holder from person | camera tie-back: door events joined with entry/exit video and face-mismatch alerts
4) log integrity | local door controller logs | entries attributed to an authorized badge ID | ship logs to a tamper-evident store (WORM/signed) in real time, reconcile counts daily
5) insider facilitation | badge/credential provisioning tooling | second person with admin rights enrolls the false identity | dual-approval on new credential creation + review of all enrollments not backed by an HR record

Those rows name the control domain and the verification that catches it, without describing *how* to execute the spoof or the forgery. If this is a real incident you're compiling, I'm happy to help structure the full after-action report, the timeline, or the remediation checklist around those detection points — just not the execution detail.
